ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The $8$ eyelets for the lace of a sneaker all lie on a rectangle, four equally spaced on each of the longer sides. The rectangle has a width of $50$ mm and a length of $80$ mm. There is one eyelet at each vertex of the rectangle. The lace itself must pass between the vertex eyelets along a width side of the rectangle and then crisscross between successive eyelets until it reaches the two eyelets at the other width side of the rectrangle as shown. After passing through these final eyelets, each of the ends of the lace must extend at least $200$ mm farther to allow a knot to be tied. Find the minimum length of the lace in millimeters.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a tall vertical rectangle with four eyelets equally spaced on each of the two long vertical sides. There is a straight lace segment across the bottom width between the two lower vertex eyelets, then three X-shaped crisscross sections between successive levels, reaching the two top vertex eyelets; loose lace ends leave from the two top eyelets. Reasoning: The long side is 80 mm and has four equally spaced eyelets, so the vertical distance between successive eyelets is 80/3 mm. Each diagonal crisscross segment spans the rectangle width, 50 mm, and one vertical gap, 80/3 mm. Thus each diagonal has length sqrt(50^2 + (80/3)^2) = sqrt(2500 + 6400/9) = sqrt(28900/9) = 170/3 mm. The diagram has 6 such diagonal segments, totaling 6 * 170/3 = 340 mm. The bottom straight width segment is 50 mm, so the lace used inside the rectangle is 340 + 50 = 390 mm. The two loose ends must each extend at least 200 mm, adding 400 mm. Therefore the minimum lace length is 390 + 400 = 790 mm.
